name: Cendré Smoked Plum-Vanilla Hard Candy
description: Individually wrapped hard candies in deep purple-grey, hand-batch produced using smoked plum reduction and natural vanilla analog. Cendré is known for its muted, sophisticated flavor palette — these are not sweet-forward candies but slow, contemplative ones.
flavor_profile: Initial smoke and dried plum tartness, gradually revealing a warm vanilla depth — long, almost wine-like finish
cultural_context: A niche product with a devoted following among Tier 3 creatives and Tier 4 hobbyist food culture enthusiasts. The tin format is collectible — Cendré releases limited seasonal designs — and the candies are sometimes found at gallery openings, private salons, and high-end waiting rooms as a quiet statement of taste. Not widely known, which is considered part of the appeal.
story_hooks: Cendré's founder died six months ago and left the business to her two adult children, who disagree fundamentally on whether to scale up or keep it small — the brand is quietly fracturing.

A limited seasonal tin released in commemoration of a pre-collapse cultural event contains a hidden message in the tin's inner liner — whether it was intentional or accidental is unclear, but collectors are obsessing over it on private mesh forums.
A Tier 5 Spire resident has been anonymously bulk-ordering Cendré tins and distributing them to Tier 1 community centers — no note, no explanation — and someone is trying to find out who and why.
